title.analysis: Exact: "Never Keep Over THIS AMOUNT In a Bank (Huge Mistake)." Absolute "Never", withheld capitalized "THIS AMOUNT" and parenthetical loss warning create a specific-number curiosity gap and fear of error. "In a Bank" plausibly evokes deposit-insurance limits for some viewers, but the script never discusses FDIC coverage; the delivered answer is a personal range (3-6 months of expenses, "$15,000 to $45,000"), not one amount. Search intent overlaps "how much cash to keep in bank" and emergency-fund sizing.

script.analysis: All 19,971 stored characters read in three contiguous ranges with canonical hash match. Hook: pride in a large balance reframed as a "trap"; early subscribe CTA (~1,900 characters). Body: inflation erosion (Fed 2% target, $10K at 0.5% vs 2% inflation -> ~$9,850 real), price examples, 3-6-month expense rule ($4,000 x 3-6 = $12K-$24K), opportunity-cost example, market-crash reassurance, personal-situation caveat, cash-hoarding psychology, banks lending deposits, alternatives (index funds, half-and-half start, real estate/REITs, self-investment), emergency-size minimization, planned-purchase exception (HYSA/CDs inside 2 years), "lean cash motivates income", Parkinson framing, four-month dollar-cost-averaging plan, "$15K-$45K" sweet spot and recap. Mostly generic narration with repetitive motivational passages and no case story or on-screen data cues in text. Key omission: high-yield savings, money-market funds and T-bills paid materially above inflation in 2025, so "guaranteed to lose purchasing power" applies to low-yield accounts only; script mentions HYSA only for short-term purchases. Also omits FDIC coverage limits despite bank framing. Backup liquidity suggestions (credit cards, retirement-account loans) understate cost and plan-specific repayment risks. ASR filler ("uh", "um", "coid9") retained, not audio-verified.

claim_audit: 0:7000 $10,000 at 0.5% with 2% inflation: 10,050/1.02 = ~$9,853 real, matches ~$9,850; "1.5% per year" is the approximate real loss. Low-yield savings near 0.5% approximates national-average traditional savings, but high-yield accounts/money-market funds paid ~4% in 2025 (above ~3% CPI), so the "guaranteed loss" is account-dependent. Chipotle $8 -> $12 and new-car $38K -> $48K are rough and unsourced; widely reported car figures are average transaction prices, not medians.

0:7000 $30,000 at 7% for 10 years = ~$59,015, slightly below "over $60,000"; "$31,000" implies ~0.33%/year. At a 4% high-yield rate the 10-year balance is ~$44,400, so the gap is ~$14,600, not ~$30,000. S&P 500 "October 2024 to recent months over 15%" is a short window chosen after the fact, ambiguous dating, not evidence about future returns.

7000:14000 "Real emergencies are usually small" and job loss "rarely requires" large withdrawals are unsupported generalizations; unemployment insurance replaces only part of wages with state caps, and severance is not guaranteed. Credit-card bridging can carry ~20%+ APR; retirement-plan loans depend on plan rules and may come due on job separation. Banks lending deposits at higher rates is a fair simplification.

14000:19971 Parkinson's original law concerns work expanding to fill time; the expenditure version ("Parkinson's second law") is an adage, not a behavioral-economics finding; the extension to cash balances is asserted. "Less cash makes you more motivated" unsupported. Four-month 25% transfers is a reasonable gradual plan. $15K-$45K sweet spot equals 6 months of $2,500-$7,500 monthly expenses, internally consistent but not one amount. No FDIC $250K-per-depositor-per-bank-per-ownership-category discussion despite the bank title.
